title: Put Off Anxiety, Put On Thanksgiving
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: There's no neutral ground in the heart. Paul doesn't just say stop being anxious. He says replace anxiety with prayer and thanksgiving.
exhortation: We had the privilege of growing up with a godly dad who taught us the simple biblical idea of put off and put on. There is no neutral ground in our hearts, no no-man's-land where they coast. They're either speeding up or slowing down. And the idea is this: if you want to get rid of something, you have to replace it with something else.
Picture a blue elephant with pink polka dots. Got it? Fix it in your mind. Now stop thinking about it. Could you? Only if you replaced it with something else.

That's what Paul is telling us to do. He doesn't just say, "Stop being anxious." He says to put off anxiety by putting on prayer and thanksgiving. Do you feel anxiety creeping in? Start thanking God. Thank him that the sun came up. Thank him for food and shelter. Thank him for saving you and dying in your place. Then tell him about your anxiety and your troubles. Then thank him for listening and for being with you every step of the way. Call it a thankfulness sandwich.
Do this, and you will find that the peace of God guards your heart and mind, and the command to rejoice in the Lord becomes a natural response to a God so full of steadfast love toward us.
prayer: Lord, there are so many polka-dotted elephants that could fill our minds and take over the day. But we desire to know Christ and him crucified above all. Fill us with your Spirit and help us seek you afresh.

Bring scripture to mind for everyone listening as they go through their day. Let their hearts and minds be filled with the riches of your glory given to us in Christ Jesus, and let that dominate our thinking today. Fill us with your Spirit and a supernatural joy that people who don't know you will notice and ask, "What is it that you have?" Lord, we love you. Thank you.
